google_reviews.text: Beautiful, well curated museum with a diverse collection of paintings from many different time periods, styles and regions. A little bit of something for everyone. To top it off the sculpture garden surrounding the museum is a great way to start or finish your experience.

Maybe it was because our first visit coincided with an Eagles game, or the beautiful fall weather that there were no crowds to contend with, leaving us to enjoy the museum at our own pace. The permanent exhibits provided a great opportunity to view multiple pieces by Sloan and Pyle as well as the excellent temporary exhibits on Illustrating Race, and Plant Photography.

Beautiful museum located in a charming neighborhood. I went on an autumn evening and was greeted by warm and friendly staff. The collections are GORGEOUS and focus on the golden age of illustration and the Pre-Raphaelites which is so wonderful to see. The museum is a great size and can be done in a few hours and has a sculpture garden as well (can't wait to visit in the spring). Everyone I met there was so kind, from those at the front desk to the person running the gift shop. Can't wait to visit again

I still love this place. The second time around is even better. The staff is so sweet and helpful. Bring a sweater. It's freezing inside!

Highly recommend this place. I discovered new American artists and enjoyed artwork that told stories (thanks to well written historical summaries), made me feel curious, happy, and inspired wonder.

The small-ish museum is located on gorgeous land with trails, greens, picnic areas. And if you want even more, head over to nearby Rockford Park.

Even though there were no tours on the Saturday I went, the sweet person from whom I bought the tix was so knowledgeable. I really appreciate that she understood my frustration with the website and shared that similar feedback has already been shared with IT. She also suggested other area museums I may enjoy based on my preferences.
Fantastic museum for fans of the Pre-Raphaelites. The museum is small, but thoughtfully curated with a diverse collection. The exhibit on illustration was very unique.

museums.content_summary: The Delaware Art Museum in Wilmington is a must for art lovers who want big ideas without big-city crowds. It’s best known for a remarkable concentration of British Pre-Raphaelite art and an outstanding suite of works tied to illustrator Howard Pyle and the Brandywine tradition. Calm galleries, thoughtfully curated displays, and an inviting campus make it easy to slow down and really look—ideal for travelers building a day around close, immersive encounters with painting, illustration, and American modernism.
museums.content_description:
**Delaware Art Museum** offers one of the most rewarding “surprise” collections in the Mid-Atlantic—especially if you’re drawn to narrative painting, poetic symbolism, and the craft of illustration. The museum’s signature strength is its exceptional holding of British *Pre-Raphaelite* and Victorian-era art, where you can linger over jewel-like color, medieval revival themes, and meticulous natural detail associated with artists such as **Dante Gabriel Rossetti**, **John Everett Millais**, and **Edward Burne-Jones** (works and related material may appear across painting, works on paper, and design). This focus gives the museum a distinctive identity that feels more London than Delaware—yet grounded in Wilmington’s own collecting history.

Just as compelling is the museum’s deep connection to American illustration through **Howard Pyle**—a pivotal figure who shaped the golden age of illustration and taught artists who helped define the Brandywine region’s visual storytelling legacy. Expect galleries that celebrate *illustration* as fine art: dynamic compositions, dramatic lighting, and character-driven narratives that bridge popular culture and museum-worthy technique.

Architecturally and experientially, the visit is designed for art enthusiasts: **light-filled, comfortable galleries**, clear sightlines, and a pace that encourages close looking rather than rushing. Plan time to explore rotating exhibitions and to recharge between galleries—this is a museum that rewards repeat visits, especially if you enjoy tracing how symbolism, narrative, and design threads connect Victorian Britain to American artistic modernity.
content_highlights: Notable concentration of British Pre-Raphaelite and Victorian art (including key figures such as Rossetti, Millais, and Burne-Jones)
Howard Pyle holdings that foreground American illustration as a serious, museum-grade art form
Brandywine-region storytelling tradition and the wider legacy of Pyle’s students and followers
Visitor-friendly galleries with an intimate, uncrowded viewing experience ideal for close looking
Rotating exhibitions that add fresh context around narrative art, design, and works on paper

google_reviews.text: We took our kids here recently and they loved it (5 and 2 years old). It is small but lots of things to look at, learn about, and touch. When we went into the Dino area an employee came over with a chest and let us look at some real fossils! Very cool. Everyone was kind and helpful. We walked some of the trial but didn't do any of the group lead activities this time. We will definitely be back.

First time visiting this place. We went with my family as a field trip since they are home schooled. I was very impressed with the exhibits and the layout. The building is not huge but they really cover a lot in there. They have it broken down into section, with various geographical locations specified. When we were there they had an animatronic dinosaur exhibit on display. There was also a room where the kids could see a live turtle, snake and tarantula. They have a nice gift shop and also a place to eat. Admission was around $30 per person. There is an outdoor area as well but it was raining when we were there.

I visited from out of state. I can say that it was very cool! It's small but has a ton of awesome things! You can learn so much from here. A bunch of educational things along with taxidermy animals to give a feel of what the animal is like. They also have an outdoor area I didn't get to go to but definitely will if we ever come back! There is also an awesome little nook room. Great for younger kids. Has live animals, toys, a cave and books! Only thing I wish is the cafe had more options. Though overall amazing experience and would recommend! Super nice employees I must add!

Nice museum. Great staff.
Staff welcomesld well and explained in detail what can be done here. Tickets price is as listed in the website. No reservation required as crowd is less even on public holiday. Paying ticket price with cash, we get discount.
Immediate right after the entrance is restroom. This museum is small. They have all varieties of animals.

Some fossils are real and some are man made by experts with their research on actual fossils.

They explained about the history of the museum and effort that scientists spent on fossils.

They have food available inside to purchase. Outside seating is also available to have our own food.
The trail at the back the museum is ok but nothing much there.
If we've interest on plants, they listed the names the grown there.

Parking is free and plenty available. Lots of pictures can be taken outside itself with the animal statues outside. Kids love them.

Inside, they have audio at each attraction to make it real, even though the fossils are not which is very nice.

We should watch for each animal they listed as some are not visible unless we notice them as they were designed pretty awesome which shows their 100% efforts.

Amazing, kid friendly museum. Lots of interactive exhibits.  Well worth the cost of admission. The staff was friendly. Everything was clean. They gad a room ig someone needed a sensory break. The staff were great with kids and adults. The rooms were distinctive, but felt well put together.

museums.content_summary: The Delaware Museum of Natural History offers a dynamic exploration of the natural world, featuring engaging exhibits and a rich collection of fossils, minerals, and live animals. With a commitment to education and conservation, this museum provides a unique experience that ignites curiosity in visitors of all ages.
museums.content_description:
**The Delaware Museum of Natural History** invites curious minds to explore the wonders of the natural world through an impressive array of exhibits and interactive experiences. Established in 1972, this museum has positioned itself as a leading hub for environmental education and scientific research. Its **collections include over 100,000 specimens**, encompassing everything from rare fossils and *exquisite minerals* to captivating wildlife. Visitors can marvel at the intricacies of various ecosystems through immersive displays that not only showcase the beauty of nature but also emphasize the importance of conservation efforts. This commitment to environmental education makes a visit here not just enriching but also essential for understanding our planet's biodiversity. A must-see is the museum's signature exhibit featuring live animals, which provides a thrilling and educational glimpse into the lives of various species in their natural habitats. This interactive aspect ensures that children and adults alike leave the museum inspired by the beauty and complexity of life on Earth. 

 Further enhancing the visitor experience, the museum is located within a serene park setting that invites exploration beyond its walls. **The architecture itself** is designed to harmonize with the surrounding landscape, creating a tranquil environment where learning continues outdoors. Beautifully landscaped gardens complement the museum’s goals of promoting environmental awareness and stewardship. Throughout the year, the museum conducts programs and workshops, ensuring that every visit offers something fresh and engaging, from seasonal exhibitions to guided tours that deepen knowledge and appreciation of the natural world. Whether you’re a local or a traveler passing through Wilmington, **the Delaware Museum of Natural History** promises an unforgettable adventure that will spark your sense of discovery and celebration of nature.
content_highlights: Diverse collection of over 100,000 specimens
Immersive exhibits featuring local and global ecosystems
Live animal exhibits showcasing species in natural habitats
Commitment to environmental education and conservation
Stunning gardens and outdoor learning spaces

museums.content_summary: Visit the **Historic Odessa Foundation** to step back in time and explore the rich cultural heritage of early 19th-century Delaware. Nestled in the charming town of Odessa, this unique museum features a collection of restored historic buildings, stunning gardens, and engaging exhibits that showcase the life, craftsmanship, and artistry of the period. Experience history come alive in a picturesque setting!
museums.content_description:
**Historic Odessa Foundation** is a remarkable destination that transports visitors to the heart of early American history. Located in the quaint town of Odessa, Delaware, this museum is comprised of a series of beautifully restored structures, including the iconic *Walnut Hall* and the *Daniel Wagoner House*. Each building is a testament to the region's craftsmanship and colonial heritage, providing a glimpse into the daily lives and surroundings of the 19th century. The foundation's commitment to historic preservation makes it a unique resource for those interested in architecture and history alike.  

As you stroll through the meticulously maintained grounds, you will encounter enchanting gardens that reflect the era's aesthetic sensibilities. The museum offers interactive exhibits and informative tours that invite guests to engage with the rich narratives of those who lived and worked in these homes. Special events and workshops throughout the year provide hands-on experiences, from crafting traditional goods to learning about period gardening techniques.  

Visiting the **Historic Odessa Foundation** is not just about observing history; it’s about feeling it. With each step through its beautifully preserved corridors, you can almost hear the whispers of the past, making this an unmissable stop for history buffs, families, and anyone drawn to the inspiration of bygone eras. Don't miss the opportunity to immerse yourself in the cultural tapestry that defines this enchanting locale!
content_highlights: Multiple restored historic buildings showcasing 19th-century architecture
Enchanting gardens that bring period aesthetics to life
Interactive exhibits detailing daily life in early America
Engaging special events and workshops throughout the year
Insightful guided tours led by knowledgeable staff

google_reviews.text: You won’t find a better holiday tour of the historic houses than this!  It’s an amazing opportunity to see the interiors of some homes that date back to the 1700’s.  The individual decor is exceptional and the Christmas ideas are beautifully executed.  There are almost two dozen spaces to experience so plan for the entire day!

# A Tale of Two Experiences in Odessa, DE

I must begin by noting that our initial experience was quite different from our recent visit.

Our adventure began with the intention of letting our children explore the charming town of Odessa, DE. We stopped by the HOF to gather some information, and upon entering the building, we discovered a cooking expo in progress, which we eagerly joined. The ladies hosting the event were friendly and knowledgeable. Shortly after, we were advised to head outside and around back to see the “kitchen garden.” As we approached the garden, a tour guide approached us, inviting us to join a tour that was already underway. We were thrilled at the opportunity for our children to see the interiors of the houses. The tour was meant to cover three separate homes, and we learned that the guide had already completed two and was starting the third when we joined.

We proceeded to the Corbin House to continue the tour. As we began, more visitors joined, bringing our group to about a dozen, which made the spaces feel quite crowded. Despite this, we managed to go along with it, although I was unaware of any costs associated with this particular tour. I assumed it would be a worst-case scenario of $10 per person due to past experiences. However, had I not been familiar with the past tour, I wouldn’t have realized there was even a fee until well into the tour, and even then, the pricing felt somewhat ambiguous rather than fixed.

After touring the Corbin House, we informed the tour guide—who was very pleasant and knowledgeable—that we intended to end our visit there to grab a bite to eat, which was our original plan before the tour. I mentioned I would return to the office to settle the payment, and he instructed me to tell the office staff that our group had only completed one house, which I assumed had to do with pricing.

When I entered the office to pay, I was shocked to learn that the cost was $15 per person for my group of five, totaling $75 for just one house on an overcrowded tour. This unexpected price left me astonished, and as a result, I opted not to dine at the local Cantwell Tavern, which had been my initial reason for stopping in town. Be cautious of the pricing—although the listed price online is $10, don’t be surprised by a higher bill and a significant chunk of your afternoon wasted.

~Odin your local guild extraordinaire
Find me on Twitch = BlackwaterOdin

Breathtaking Ceremony at Historic Odessa's Corbit-Sharp House!

We chose Historic Odessa's Corbit-Sharp House for our wedding ceremony, and it surpassed our wildest dreams! The picturesque grounds, steeped in history and charm, provided the perfect backdrop for our special day.

Megan and Jennifer, were exceptional. Megan guided us through every step through rehearsal and the day of, ensuring a seamless experience. Her attention to detail and kindness were invaluable. When I had a last-minute dress malfunction, Megan appeared with needle and thread, saving the day and then making sure we took a moment to breathe!

The historic grounds were immaculately maintained, with stunning gardens and architecture. The ceremony space was breathtaking, with ample room for our guests and beautiful backdrops for photos.

If you're seeking a romantic, historic setting for your ceremony, look no further than Historic Odessa's Corbit-Sharp House. They will ensure your day is unforgettable, surrounded by timeless elegance and beauty.

We did a guided..? Tour the second to last weekend in December of 2017. Our tour guide brought us through 3 historic homes and told us that they were decorated for  christmas which we were excited to see. We kept getting told to "come back in the spring/fall or any other time" to get a good tour of the homes. We were with about 10 other people confused as to why we weren't getting the "good" tour since we had paid $10 a person to be told "this is a historic room" or "there's a ton of information about this house" but you have to come back to find out. If we were on the (bring you through old homes but not give you any facts or be able to answer any questions accurately) tour they should better advertise that before paying. Very disappointing. Our tour guide was poorly trained on information as well. Loved to see the history but that is all we did, a quick glance through. There were rooms we were also told we could not go into because every other time of the year they give thorough tours but not the one we were on. Wish we knew we had to "come at a different time".

My niece had her baby shower here! It was the perfect setting and fit all the guests properly with room to walk around and mingle.

The food and drinks were served buffet style in another room, which was nice too! They had a coffee & tea station with decorative urns to self-service. The food was AMAZING! Everything was really good, most guests went back for seconds 😉

The building is old but has lots of character. The front room has big windows for lots of natural sun light 🌞 very cozy. The front door and entryway reminds me of an old farmhouse painting, that's been weathered and torn for decades.
There is a small coatroom rack to the left side hallway and a few updated bathrooms that are private, as well as equipped for the handicap!

I believe they can hold up to 70 guests-  so if you are interested, this place is certainly very charming!!!

google_reviews.text: My wife and I did the tour today when in town and it was so much fun. The tour guide, Jackie, was so nice and beyond knowledgeable about the town and buildings. The buildings were so beautiful and authentic. It was like stepping back into time. The town itself and so amazing.

A very nice starting point for your New Castle visit. Spoke with Mike, a local volunteer who ran me through all the center had to offer and showed me the excellent video. Everything you need to get the most from your visit is here!

A bike ride exploring one of the Delaware Greenways to Historic New Castle,  founded by Dutch settlers in the 1650s along the Delaware river provides a step back into history. William Penn first set foot in Battery Park. An historic sign state “He proceeded to the fort and performed livery of seizin, he took the key, therefof,… we did deliver unto him 1 Turf with a twig upon it, a porringer with river water and soil, in part of all”. The gifts symbolized his proprietorship of Pennsylvania which at that time included the three lower counties that became the state of Delaware, “the first state”.
We visited 2 homes and were given very informative tours. The houses were furnished and have an idea of what they would use.

This is one of the oldest spots in the US. Nearby, William Penn and co landed. This is one of the earliest settlements in the Americas. It makes sense to explore and learn more about this chapter of history while you're there. Make sure to visit offices of the Historical Society and ask for some additional information and resources. You could also talk to them about organizing tours. They'll have some great stuff for you which you otherwise would not have gotten to learn about!

museums.content_summary: Discover the rich tapestry of history at the **New Castle Historical Society**, a unique gem that offers visitors a deep dive into Delaware's past through engaging exhibits, historic buildings, and immersive experiences. This museum promises a captivating journey for history enthusiasts and casual visitors alike.
museums.content_description:
**New Castle Historical Society** is a beautifully preserved institution dedicated to telling the story of New Castle, Delaware, from its earliest days as a colonial port to its significance in American history. The museum is housed within some of the city's oldest structures, providing an authentic ambiance that enhances your exploration of the past. Visitors will find themselves surrounded by vibrant exhibits that showcase a mix of artifacts, photographs, and documents that portray the lives and events that shaped this historic town. The society's commitment to historic preservation makes it an essential stop for anyone intrigued by the interplay of architecture and history. This is a place where stories come alive, and visitors can truly experience the essence of 18th-century America.  

  Exploring the museum's extensive collection is like stepping back in time. You’ll encounter displays on local figures, revolutionary battles, and daily life during different eras. The architectural features of the museum itself reflect the period in which it was built, offering a window into the past with every corner you turn. Don't miss the special programs and events, designed to give you an enriching experience that includes guided tours, lectures, and hands-on activities that engage all ages. With its welcoming atmosphere and a wealth of knowledge, the **New Castle Historical Society** stands as a testament to preserving history for future generations, inviting you to uncover Delaware's unique heritage.
content_highlights: Historic buildings reflecting 18th-century architecture
Engaging exhibits on Delaware's colonial and revolutionary history
Vast collection of local artifacts and documents
Interactive programs for all ages
Expert-led guided tours that bring history to life

They did a beautiful job with the show this year and in my opinion it was the best one yet. Even more awesome....I won first place in the beginners category this year!! This is a nice little museum highlighting up and coming artists from all areas. For admission, they only ask for a small donation, with the minimum asking being $12. Since the place is small, you can spend at least an hour here looking at all of the fascinating exhibits. The museum itself is very clean and well organized. They have a large parking area, coat check area, restroom and a small gift shop near the entrance. I enjoyed my visit and would definitely recommend it to anyone who loves art.

A nice but small contemporary art museum. Tickets cost $7. It was worth the price, enjoyed the exhibits — the theme was on AI and art, and I liked the perspective they shared. It’s downtown right next to the River walk, so easy to hit that after.

I love museums and galleries, and in recent times, I have been looking for something more manageable since I am not always able to walk as far or as long as other friends and family members. I want to mention this for any visitors who may bring along an elderly relative or someone with an illness or restrictions to their movements.

With this in mind, I must say this museum was comfortable and easy to navigate. I couldn't believe they didn't charge entry but simply recommended donations. I think it's worth the trip and donations to keep this valuable resource in the community! By the way, they have a store where I honestly had to stop myself from buying too many things.

As far as the art being showcased this season, it had interesting installations and interactives from 16 artists. I felt it called upon our curiosity and open-mindedness to observe and understand some of the topics woven through the art. I will admit this was a good experience for me because I'm not typically a fan of contemporary art.

I wanted to open myself up to new experiences. Trying to understand what some artists are trying to bring to our attention made for a good afternoon and great conversation after my husband and I left. I look forward to checking out upcoming exhibits this year and maybe visiting during an art loop.

museums.content_summary: Set in Wilmington’s creative riverfront district, The Delaware Contemporary is the state’s hub for living artists and ideas in motion. Rather than a permanent trove, it shines through rotating exhibitions—often spotlighting regional talent alongside wider contemporary currents—so repeat visits pay off. Expect a clean, gallery-forward setting with an intimate scale that encourages close looking, plus opportunities to encounter new media, installation, and experimental work without the crowds of a major metro museum.
museums.content_description:
**The Delaware Contemporary** is Wilmington’s go-to stop for art lovers who prefer the thrill of what’s happening *now* over encyclopedic history. With a **modest permanent collection** and a **competent curatorial program**, the museum’s strength is its **rotating exhibitions**—a changing mix that frequently elevates Delaware and mid-Atlantic artists while engaging broader conversations in *contemporary art*, *installation*, and *new media*. For travelers, that means a visit feels timely and specific: you’re not checking off canonical masterpieces so much as encountering fresh work, new voices, and ambitious experiments.

Architecturally, the experience is intentionally streamlined: **bright, flexible gallery spaces** designed to adapt to different scales—from intimate works on paper to room-filling installations. The museum’s manageable footprint rewards slow looking; you can give serious attention to each show without museum fatigue. Expect clear sightlines, uncluttered presentation, and the kind of pacing that suits contemporary work—where ideas unfold across series, materials, and formats.

For visitors, the best strategy is to arrive curious and leave time to discuss what you’ve seen. Check the current exhibition list before you go so you can target what resonates—whether it’s concept-driven painting, lens-based work, or immersive environments. As a regional contemporary center, it’s an excellent complement to historic Wilmington sites: a focused, modern counterpoint that keeps your itinerary rooted in the present tense.
content_highlights: Rotating contemporary exhibitions with frequent emphasis on Delaware and regional artists
Flexible, white-cube-style galleries suited to installation, multimedia, and experimental work
A visit format that’s easy to do thoroughly—ideal for close looking without crowds
Programs and presentations that foreground living artists and current art-world conversations
A strong “return visit” museum: new shows regularly refresh what you’ll see

museums.content_summary: The **Winterthur Museum & Country Estate** is a captivating destination that immerses visitors in the grandeur of America's decorative arts. With its remarkable collection of over 90,000 objects, stunning gardens, and an estate that echoes the elegance of a bygone era, this museum offers a unique journey through history that combines beauty, education, and tranquility. Prepare to be enchanted by the artful landscapes and the stories they tell.
museums.content_description:
**Winterthur Museum & Country Estate** is not just a museum; it is a harmonious blend of art, history, and nature that invites guests to explore the richness of American decorative arts. Set amidst a sprawling 1,000-acre estate, the museum showcases the exquisite collection of Henry Francis du Pont, who dedicated his life to preserving and celebrating American craftsmanship. The collection features iconic pieces from the *Colonial period* through the *20th century*, with an emphasis on furniture, textiles, and ceramics that reflect the evolution of style and design. Each object tells a story, providing insights into the cultural history of America and the influences of both *European* and *American* artisanship. Visitors can take guided tours through the elegantly furnished rooms of the mansion, which are beautifully presented to reflect the du Pont family's way of life. These intimate spaces bring the past to life with their authentic decor and intriguing narratives.   

   The beauty of **Winterthur** extends beyond its impressive interiors; the estate is also home to award-winning gardens that are meticulously designed and ever blooming. Guests can stroll through the *Enchanted Woods*, an interactive garden designed for children, or savor the breathtaking views from the *Longwood Gardens*, featuring an array of seasonal plantings that celebrate the artistry of horticulture. Seasonal events and exhibitions provide additional opportunities for engagement and learning, making every visit a new experience. With its dedication to preserving and presenting cultural heritage in a stunningly gorgeous setting, **Winterthur Museum & Country Estate** promises an enriching escape for art lovers, history buffs, and families alike.
content_highlights: Extensive collection of American decorative arts featuring over 90,000 objects
Beautifully restored mansion showcasing 18th and 19th-century furnishings
Stunning 1,000-acre estate with award-winning gardens
Unique seasonal exhibitions and events that enhance visitor experience
Interactive garden designed specifically for children

museums.content_description:
Set in downtown Dover, the **Biggs Museum of American Art** is a satisfying destination for travelers who enjoy exploring the breadth of American creativity in a museum that feels personal rather than sprawling. Its scale encourages close looking—time to linger over brushwork, materials, and the storytelling power of American subjects—while rotating exhibitions add a sense of discovery for repeat visitors.

The museum’s strengths typically center on **American art and material culture**, spotlighting the kinds of works that shaped visual life in the United States: portraiture, landscape traditions, and objects where design and craftsmanship matter as much as imagery. For art enthusiasts, this is a place to tune your eye to the evolution of American taste—how *representation*, *regional identity*, and *craft* intersect across different periods. Because the collection is modest, curatorial choices tend to be focused and readable, making it an excellent museum for visitors who like clear themes and well-paced galleries.

Architecturally and experientially, **Biggs** rewards a relaxed visit: it’s easy to pair with a day exploring Dover’s historic core, and the museum’s manageable size makes it ideal for a focused one- to two-hour stop. Plan to give yourself extra time for special exhibitions and any public programs—often the best way to connect local context to the art on view, and to leave with a sharper sense of Delaware’s place within the larger American visual tradition.
content_highlights: A concentrated, approachable survey of American art—ideal for close looking and themed gallery walks
Rotating exhibitions that bring fresh perspectives and encourage return visits
An emphasis on craftsmanship and material culture alongside fine art traditions
A quiet, uncrowded viewing experience in the heart of downtown Dover
Easy to combine with Dover’s historic sites for a full culture-focused day trip

google_reviews.text: It's nice but small art museum. But it's expending in next two yr. And it's free to visit. I learned some history here. Parking is plenty near by less than 0.1-0.3 miles.  Look the photo of city map with " P" to park for free.

This museum is 100% worth a stop if you're in Delaware. There are different exhibits on the 2nd and 3rd floors, each with their own charm and beauty. Going through it at a leisurely pace will take an hour of well spent time. And it's free!

I was truly impressed and inspired. There were 3 floors of exhibitions and they each took me to a different space and time. I definitely left there wanting to be involved and present.
Had the best time . Staff were very helpful and knowledgeable as this was my first visit. Can’t wait to go back.

museums.content_summary: The Hagley Museum and Library in Wilmington offers visitors a unique insight into the legacy of American innovation and industry. Set on the picturesque banks of the Brandywine River, this museum allows guests to discover the history of the DuPont company, explore beautifully preserved mill structures, and immerse themselves in interactive exhibits that ignite curiosity about science and technology.
museums.content_description:
**Hagley Museum and Library** is not just a museum—it's a journey through America's industrial past that specifically highlights the significance of chemical research and development. Founded on the historical grounds where E.I. du Pont established his explosive business in 1802, this museum offers a unique blend of history and science. The lush landscape, accentuated by stunning views of the Brandywine River, provides an extraordinary backdrop to explore the innovative spirit of one of America’s most renowned families. The museum encapsulates a fantastic array of historical buildings, including the **DuPont Black Powder Mills**, where visitors can see the transformative processes of industry in action. Experience how early American ingenuity laid the foundation for modern science and technology through engaging displays and live demonstrations.  

For visitors, **Hagley Museum and Library** fosters an interactive learning environment, ideal for families and science enthusiasts alike. Explore the *science of innovation* through hands-on exhibits that cover everything from chemical experiments to environmental studies. The library, with its extensive collection of manuscripts and archives, enhances the experience, providing those interested in research the opportunity to delve further into the rich history of American enterprise. Make sure to visit the beautiful gardens and picturesque walking trails, which seamlessly blend natural beauty with the legacy of industry. With its rich offerings, **Hagley Museum and Library** is a must-see destination for anyone eager to understand the impact of science on our daily lives.
content_highlights: Historic DuPont Black Powder Mills
Stunning landscapes along the Brandywine River
Interactive science exhibits for all ages
Extensive library of American business history
Educational programs and live demonstrations

google_reviews.text:
Found Hagley on a whim as we were planning a quick overnight to DE and boy am I glad I did. We arrived late on Saturday and didn’t realize how expansive the property was and all it had to offer.

We opted to take a house tour which was extremely interesting, informative and really fascinating to learn about the DuPont family and how the house evolved over time. Our 10 year old son was fascinated and the staff were so knowledgeable, enthusiastic and kind.

Since we only got to see a small portion we ended up going back the next day to see the powder mills and demonstrations as well as the inventions and patents in the visitor building. Our son was so fascinated and really learn how the Industrial Revolution evolved.

The woman at the powder mill demonstration was an absolute gem. I forget her name but she’d been there for 17 years and was just so sweet. She was excited to show us the demo and shared a wealth of knowledge about how they really utilized the Brandywine to turn water into power. Seeing the machinery come to life was amazing.

The property is expansive with so many things to see and do. Staff is superb, really wanting you to learn in a fun and engaging way. Highly recommend a stop. This property is truly more than just the Du Pont family history and has something for everyone.

Great place to visit. Came around 3pm, only the two of us on the shuttle to the Du Pont house. The tour guides are wonderful and even the shuttle driver was great, gave us very informative introduction to the historic site. People who work here to really care about the history and the legacy of the Du Pont family. Can’t wait to come back here again!
A peaceful stroll through Hagley Museum end of September.. Beautiful scenery with river, rapids, n falls.. Informative displays and demonstrations. A Lot of local History. A Must see.

We didn't expect to spend as much time as we did, and wish we had spent more time than we did.  The initial display of inventions set the stage for the DuPont story. That, and an entrepreneurial spirit were on display at this museum.
The tour of the mansion was informative  and demonstrated house remodeling is not new.  The cars and carriages were nice for a small collection. My favorite part of the "museum" was the demonstration of water turbine driven metal working equipment.  I also liked the models of the making of gun powder, and the demonstration of how gun powder was tested for quality.
I highly recommend this museum that is located in a beautiful setting.

Wow! Just terrific place. I had no idea what to expect, and unfortunately did come early enough to explore the second floor. The vibrancy, colors, layout and lighting make this place eye candy. It's such an appealing way for adults and children to learn about innovation, invention and patents with real patent models. Highly recommend.   Come learn about improving the mousetrap, toilet, hairbrush and everything else. It's obvious that lots of money, time and thought is invested to make this place inviting for everyone.
